newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open stronger in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open stronger in active trading.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened stronger for a third straight session on Thursday with a host of factors including a firmer dollar and tame U.S. economic data helping to boost prices

"People are a little bit more positive on Canada than they were, say, a few days ago and in turn it's helping us carry it on. We've been very busy," said one T-bill trader with a bank-owned brokerage.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.29 percent from 3.35 percent at the close of trading on Wednesday.

Canada's dollar strengthened past C$1.38 (US$0.7246) in overnight trading as investors in the Far East continued to show good interest to buy the currency. The stronger dollar has helped reduce speculation that the Bank of Canada would soon hike interest rates.
Tame U.S. GDP data out this morning also provided support for the market.

"It's definitely put us in a good positive tone. We're hoping people will come back. We really have not seen tons of clients in the long end. A lot of the rally has been short covering and dealer driven," the dealer said.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.62 percent from 3.69 percent on Wednesday. The one-year when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 4.14 percent from 4.18 percent.

The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.40 percent, in the upper half of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.5 percent target range. The rise in call was attributed to normal settlement pressures from Tuesday's weekly T-bill tender.
